questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She had a _____ for creating beautiful artwork.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**talent**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**talent**" refers to a natural ability or skill, especially in a particular area such as art, music, or sports. (प्रतिभा)
 
• In the sentence, "She had a _____ for creating beautiful artwork," the word "talent" correctly conveys the idea of her innate ability to produce art.
 
• The other options do not fit semantically in the context of having a natural gift or ability.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *She had a talent__ for creating beautiful artwork.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Mode (मोड/प्रकार)**: Refers to a manner or way in which something occurs or is experienced, not suitable in this context.
 
• **Post (पद)**: Refers to a job or position, especially in employment or official capacity, which is irrelevant here.
 
• **Trigger (उद्दीपन/घटना का कारण बनना)**: Refers to something that initiates an event or reaction, not a fit for describing an innate skill.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase.

Reading between the lines

options.text: Understanding a deeper or hidden meaning
Avoiding reading and engaging in gossips

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Reading between the lines"** means understanding a deeper or hidden meaning that is not explicitly stated. (गुप्त या छिपे हुए अर्थ को समझना)

 
 
• **Example:** While the report seemed positive, reading between the lines revealed some concerning trends.
 
 
 
• **"Deeper or hidden meaning"** refers to the interpretation or significance that is not immediately obvious or explicitly mentioned. (गहरा या छिपा हुआ अर्थ)
 
 
• **Example:** She read between the lines of his cheerful words and sensed his underlying sadness.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: Avoiding reading and engaging in gossips** (पढ़ाई से बचना और गपशप में शामिल होना): This option refers to evading the act of reading and instead indulging in idle talk or rumors.

 
 
• **Example:** He spends most of his time avoiding reading and engaging in gossips about his colleagues.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Taking things literally** (चीजों को शब्दशः लेना): Refers to interpreting words or phrases in their most basic sense without considering their figurative or hidden meanings.
 
 
• **Example:** He took the joke literally and completely missed the humor.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Reading a book** (किताब पढ़ना): Refers to the act of engaging with written material, such as a novel or textbook.
 
 
• **Example:** She spends her weekends reading a book by her favorite author.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The sudden plot twist in the story added an element of _______ that kept readers on the edge of their seats.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**ambiguity**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**ambiguity**" refers to uncertainty or inexactness of meaning in language. (अस्पष्टता)
 
• In storytelling, **ambiguity** often adds suspense and keeps readers guessing, especially when the plot takes an unexpected turn.
 
• The phrase "on the edge of their seats" implies excitement and suspense, which aligns well with the idea of **ambiguity**.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The sudden plot twist in the story added an element of ambiguity__ that kept readers on the edge of their seats.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Redundancy (अत्यधिकता)**: Refers to unnecessary repetition, which would make a story dull, not exciting.
 
• **Monotony (एकरसता)**: Means a lack of variety and interest; dullness. This contradicts the idea of keeping readers engaged.
 
• **Predictability (पूर्वानुमेयता)**: Refers to something that can be easily guessed; it would reduce suspense, not increase it.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The soldiers / sacrifice their lives / to guarding / the nation and its boundaries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**sacrifice**" should be followed by the infinitive form "**to guard**" and not the gerund form "**to guarding**."
 
• The correct construction is: "**sacrifice their lives to guard** the nation..."
 
• Using "to guarding" is incorrect because "to" here functions as part of the infinitive marker, not a preposition.
 
• Hence, the grammatical error lies in **segment 3**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The soldiers sacrifice their lives **to guard** the nation and its boundaries."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The soldiers"** – Grammatically correct subject of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "the nation and its boundaries"** – This is a correct prepositional phrase acting as the object of the verb.
 
• **Option 4: "sacrifice their lives"** – This is a correct verb phrase with a clear meaning.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The dog / eager wagged / its tail when / it saw its owner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**eager wagged**" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct usage should be "**eagerly wagged**" as an **adverb** (eagerly) is needed to modify the verb "wagged".
 
• Adjectives like "eager" describe nouns, not actions, so they cannot be used directly before a verb without a linking verb.
 
• Hence, the error lies in **segment 3**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The dog **eagerly wagged** its tail when it saw its owner."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: "It saw its owner"** – Correct clause in past tense.
 
• **Option 4: "its tail when"** – Grammatically correct phrase as part of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Roma was __the dearest child to her mother.__

options.text: At sixes and sevens with her parents
The apple of her parents’ eyes
The star of her parents’ eyes
The body and soul of her parents

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. The apple of her parents’ eyes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"dearest"** means someone who is loved the most or cherished highly. (सबसे प्रिय)

 
 
• **Example:** My grandmother always called me her dearest grandchild.
 
 
 
• **"The apple of one’s eye"** is an idiom that refers to someone who is cherished, adored, or loved deeply by another person. (आंखों का तारा)
 
 
• **Example:** Little Mia is the apple of her father’s eye.
 
 
 
• Hence, the phrase "Roma was the dearest child to her mother" can be replaced with "Roma was the apple of her parents’ eyes."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. The apple of her parents’ eyes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: At sixes and sevens with her parents** (उलझन में): Refers to a state of confusion or disorder.

 
 
• **Example:** After the argument, the siblings were at sixes and sevens with each other.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: The star of her parents’ eyes** (आंखों का सितारा): Although similar in meaning to "apple of one’s eye," this phrase is less commonly used and does not fit the idiomatic expression as accurately.
 
 
• **Example:** Sarah was often called the star of her parents’ eyes for her accomplishments.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The body and soul of her parents** (शरीर और आत्मा): This phrase does not convey the intended meaning of someone being cherished or loved deeply; it is unrelated to the context.
 
 
• **Example:** He devoted himself to the body and soul of his work.

questions.question:
Change the following into superlative degree.

She is taller than other girls in the class.

options.text: No other girl in the class is as tall as she.
In the class she is taller than other girls.
She is tall girl in the class.
She is the tallest girl in the class.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the comparative degree: "**She is taller than other girls in the class.**"
 
• To convert it to the **superlative degree**, the structure should follow: "**She is the tallest girl in the class.**"
 
• The word "**tallest**" is the superlative form of "**tall**."
 
• This transformation compares her height to all others in the group, establishing her as having the highest degree of the quality "tall."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She is the tallest girl in the class."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "No other girl in the class is as tall as she." – This is the **positive degree** of comparison.
 
• **Option 2:** "In the class she is taller than other girls." – Still in the **comparative degree**.
 
• **Option 3:** "She is tall girl in the class." – Grammatically incorrect due to missing article ("a" or "the").

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The 100-year-old banyan was blown off in the storm last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**was blown off**" is incorrect when referring to a tree being uprooted or knocked down by a storm.
 
• The correct phrasal verb in this context is **"was blown down"**, which means to be knocked over or destroyed by wind.
 
• "Blown off" is typically used for objects being removed from a surface (e.g., the hat was blown off his head), not for trees.
 
• Therefore, the verb usage in **Option 1** contains a grammatical and contextual error.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The 100-year-old banyan was **blown down** in the storm last night."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "The 100-year-old banyan"** – Correct noun phrase describing the tree.
 
• **Option 3: "last night"** – Correct time reference in the past.
 
• **Option 4: "in the storm"** – Correct prepositional phrase indicating the cause.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. According to Mr. Sharma / the news have come / as another blow / to the family members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The noun "**news**" is an uncountable noun and is treated as singular in English grammar.
 
• Therefore, it should be followed by a singular verb, not a plural one.
 
• The phrase "**the news have come**" is incorrect. The correct form is "**the news has come**."
 
• This error lies in subject-verb agreement, where a singular subject must take a singular verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"According to Mr. Sharma, the news **has come** as another blow to the family members."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "as another blow"** – Grammatically and contextually correct.
 
• **Option 3: "According to Mr. Sharma"** – Correct reporting phrase.
 
• **Option 4: "to the family members"** – Correct prepositional phrase indicating the impact.

• **Example:** Many countries launch satellites for communication, weather forecasting, and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Correct Word:**
 
 
• **Satellites** is correctly spelled as "Satellites." The meaning remains the same. (उपग्रह)
 
• **Example:** The satellite transmitted images of the earth to the ground station.

questions.question:

The teacher __called up the class__ due to the sudden snowstorm.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **“called up”** means to phone or summon someone, which does not fit the context of cancelling a class due to a snowstorm.
 
• **“Called off”** is the correct phrasal verb meaning to cancel an event or activity.
 
• **“Called out”** means to shout or challenge someone, which is irrelevant here.
 
• **“Called on”** means to visit or to request someone to speak or act, which doesn’t convey cancellation.
 
• **“Called in”** means to summon someone to a place, like an office or meeting, not suitable for cancelling a class.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“The teacher **called off**__ the class due to the sudden snowstorm.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Call off** = to cancel something (e.g., meeting, class, event).
 
• **Call up** = to telephone or summon (e.g., military service).
 
• **Call on** = to formally request or visit.
 
• **Call out** = to challenge someone or to shout.

questions.question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

Meerut is __farthest__ from Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence compares the distance of a single place (Meerut) without contrasting it with any other specific place.
 
• In such general or neutral contexts, the use of the **positive degree** "**far**" is appropriate.
 
• "Farthest" or "farther" implies comparison, which is not clearly stated or required here.
 
• Options 3 and 4 ("more farther" and "most farthest") are incorrect due to **redundant comparative forms**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Meerut is far from Delhi."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Farther**: Used when comparing physical distance between two entities (e.g., "Meerut is farther than Ghaziabad").
 
• **Farthest**: Used when comparing three or more items in terms of distance.
 
• **Far**: Used for general statements without direct comparison.
